[yoogz] Given many people in the comments have opinions but no real lived experiences… yes, when applying for the ESTA they actually do ask for links to your social media accounts, but they are optional fields. There are in-draft laws to attempt to make it mandatory, but this is not in effect and likely won't pass Senate. The ESTA also lasts for two years and you don't need to refresh it every trip.
If you don't fill it out, they don't check it at the border either. All questions at the border were terse/direct, but nothing asked was out of the ordinary for a customs official in any country. I've had more probing questions in Canada and even Australia, prior to my citizenship.
And no, I am not white and very likely to be "targeted" by Trump

[MrFrugalSpend] For the average person, fake news bro - been there myself this year.
Social media details were optional on ETSA, they didn't look through devices.
I was asked a handful of questions like always (e.g. how long staying, purpose, return flight) for about 20 seconds … then was it.
Sure they fingerprint you then before ushering the next person through, but that's not new.
Unless you are an influencer, journalist, academic, actively campaigning anti USA / political stuff etc - unlikely to be an issue - and officially the story with a lot of them is they applied on a tourist visa, but USA class it as 'working' if you earn money out of content / writing (e.g. to film stuff for their paid social media) - so deny entry after viewing such content on the basis they believe such people are there to gather info/content to work without the appropriate visa. They don't have to give specific reasons so people assume its due to their political views. The only new question was what devices I had, I made sure I had an iphone and personal tablet only - whereas they would get interested to look deeper if people had professional content gear or a work laptop (on a tourist visa).

Terminals are usually pretty decent, especially at Newark which honestly is up there as one of my favourite hub terminals. Their LAX terminal feels pretty cramped so if possible I would fly to their IAH hub but IAH is also currently undergoing a bunch of redevelopement so pick your poison I guess.
You have 5 options to fly to NYC and you have Qantas and American usually being pretty expensive, Delta and United usually solid and Air NZ which is okay but a bit of a mess at the moment with their fleet. Qantas and Air NZ have the big advantage of no international to domestic transfer with the stopover in Auckland but given the price difference these United flights are certainly worth the hassle of dealing with a connection.
